extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, depositors of biological material, industrial property offices, depositary authorities, and patent attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory rules for depositing microorganisms/biological material under the Budapest Treaty for patent procedure, and for requesting/furnishing samples in connection with patent applications/patents. Covers timing, documentation, sample availability/restrictions, forms and practical checklists for depositors and requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for the invention to be carried out by a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general requirement (Eurasian provision cited). If biological material is involved and cannot be so described, deposit rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit requirement when biological material cannot be described
rubrics_metrics.description: If an invention involves biological material not available to the public and which cannot be described so as to enable the invention to be carried out by a person skilled in the art, the applicant must make the deposit of the biological material with a recognized depositary institution on the same terms as those laid down in the Budapest Treaty (Rule 31(1)(a) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies where the biological material is essential to enable the skilled person to carry out the invention. Equivalent requirement referenced for Eurasian applications: include evidence of deposit with a competent depositary authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of depositor/authorization when depositor ≠ applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the biological material has been deposited by a person other than the applicant, the name and address of the depositor shall be stated in the application and a document shall be submitted providing evidence that the depositor has authorized the applicant to refer to the deposited biological material and has given his unreserved and irrevocable consent to the deposited material being made available to the public (Rule 31(1)(c),(d) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This documentary evidence may be submitted within the permitted time-limits (see timing criterion). The communication is considered as constituting the unreserved and irrevocable consent of the applicant (Rule 31(2) EPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of deposit (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The deposit shall be effected no later than on the filing date of the application. Where the application claims priority and the invention requires a deposit to be sufficiently disclosed, that deposit must have been made not later than the date of filing of the previous application whose priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule is stated for both Eurasian and European procedures (Rule 11 EAPR; Rule 31(1)(a) EPC and related guidance). Ensure deposit deadlines respect priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted time-limits for submitting deposit information to EPO
rubrics_metrics.description: Information identifying the deposit (depositary institution and accession number, and where relevant depositor authorization) may be submitted within a period of 16 months after the date of filing or, if priority is claimed, after the priority date; alternatively up to the date of submission of a request for early publication; or within one month after the EPO has communicated that a right to inspection exists (Rule 31(2)(a),(b) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 16-month time limit is deemed met if the information is communicated before the technical preparations for publication of the application are completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication constitutes consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The communication of the deposit information is considered as constituting the unreserved and irrevocable consent of the applicant to the deposited biological material being made available to the public in accordance with Rule 33 EPC (Rule 31(2) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the deposit details within the permitted periods has legal effect of consent for public availability under the EPC rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO publication of recognized depositary institutions and experts
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO publishes in its Official Journal the list of depositary institutions and experts recognized for the purpose of Rules 31 to 34 EPC (Rule 33(6) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and requesters should consult the EPO list for recognized IDAs and experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for new deposit if original ceases to be available (Rule 34 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: If biological material deposited in accordance with Rule 31 EPC ceases to be available from the recognized depositary institution, a new deposit must be made with a recognized depositary institution on the same terms as those laid down in the Budapest Treaty, and a copy of the receipt of the new deposit must be forwarded to the EPO within four months of the date of the new deposit, stating the number of the European patent application or the European patent (Rule 34 EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interruption in availability is deemed not to have occurred if these conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of storage of deposited biological material is governed by Rule 9 of the Budapest Treaty and (for EPO) point 11 of bilateral agreements: at least five years after the most recent request for furnishing a sample and in any case at least thirty years after the date of deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Budapest Treaty Rule 9 and any bilateral agreements between EPO and depositary institutions for exact durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of availability of samples
rubrics_metrics.description: The deposited biological material becomes available upon request to any person from the date of publication of the patent application and to any person having the right to inspect the files pursuant to Article 128(2) EPC, prior to such date (Rule 33(1) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before publication only those with file-inspection rights can obtain samples (subject to other restrictions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on furnishing samples – undertaking by requester
rubrics_metrics.description: A sample can only be issued if the requesting party undertakes vis-à-vis the applicant or proprietor: not to make the deposited biological material or any material derived therefrom available to any third party, and to use the material or derivatives for experimental purposes only, until the application is refused/withdrawn or before the European patent has expired in the designated State in which it last expires, unless the applicant expressly waives such an undertaking (Rule 33(2) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The undertaking does not apply insofar as the requester is using the culture under a compulsory license (including ex officio licenses or use in the public interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert-only issue (Rule 32) / expert solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Until completion of the technical preparations for publication of the application, the applicant may inform the EPO that the availability of the deposited biological material is effected only by issuing a sample to an expert nominated by the requester (Rule 32(1) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mechanism to protect access until publication or, in certain cases, for set periods (see Rule 32(1)(b) wording in the Guide).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be nominated as an expert
rubrics_metrics.description: An expert may be: any natural person provided the requester furnishes evidence, when filing the request, that the nomination has the approval of the applicant; or any natural person recognized as an expert by the President of the EPO (Rule 32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet the evidence/recognition requirements when nominating an expert; confirm acceptance by applicant when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert's declaration/undertaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The nomination must be accompanied by a declaration from the expert vis-à-vis the applicant in which he enters into the undertaking pursuant to Rule 33 EPC until either the patent expires in all designated States or (where application refused/withdrawn) until the date referred to in Rule 32(1)(b) EPC (Rule 32(2) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert declaration binds the expert to the same confidentiality/usage restrictions as the requester would have had to accept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form requirements for requesting samples from the EPO
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for a sample must be submitted to the EPO on a form recognized by that Office: EPO Form 1140 (Request for issue of a sample), Form 1141 (Declaration for obtaining a sample), Form 1142 (Request for deposited material to be made available by issuing a sample to an expert). The EPO certifies on the form that a European patent application referring to the deposit has been filed and that the requester/expert is entitled to the issue of a sample. After grant the request must also be submitted to the EPO (Rule 33(4),(5) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPO transmits a copy of the request, with certification, to the depositary institution and to the patent applicant or proprietor (Rule 33(5)). Use the correct form for the route chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — check latest deposit date and start early
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the latest date by which deposit must be made; start the deposit procedure in good time (referenced sections 43–49; 53).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing is critical; allow sufficient lead time for IDA procedures and shipping (the Guide recommends starting 43–49 days earlier in examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — verify IDA can accept your microorganism
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the international depositary authority (IDA) can accept your microorganism (Guide sections 25–26; 49; 54; Section D; Rule 6.4(a)(i) and (ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different IDAs accept different organism types and have different biosafety/regulatory capacities; confirm acceptance before preparing deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — check IDA-specific requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the requirements of the IDA (Guide sections 17–22; 55; 59; Section D; Rule 6.3(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDA-specific forms, quantities, culturing conditions, packaging and fees vary; follow their published instructions carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — obtain and correctly complete required forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask for the appropriate forms; complete the forms fully and correctly and sign them (Guide paragraphs 11–15; 18; 55; Section D; Appendix 3; Rule 6.1(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete or unsigned forms can delay acceptance; use the international 'receipt' and 'viability statement' forms where mandatory (BP/4, BP/5, BP/6, BP/9 etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — designate recipient for IDA communications and patent agent details
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it clear to whom the IDA should send official communications; give the name and address of your patent agent and state if he should receive copies of the receipt and viability statement (Guide paragraphs 50–58; Rules 7; 10; 11.4(g); Article 4(1)(a); Rule 5.1(a)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity on contact points avoids lost notices; specify agent details if agent should be copied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — ensure correct form, quantity and packaging of microorganism
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure your microorganism is in the form and quantity required by the IDA and is correctly packaged (Guide paragraphs 17; 59; 27; 46; Rule 6.3(a)(i) and Rule 6.4(a)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow IDA instructions for viable cultures, stabilisation, packaging and shipping to avoid rejection or loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — do not lose the receipt and/or viability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not lose the receipt and/or viability statement (Guide paragraphs 32–39; 63).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt and viability statement are essential documents for patent prosecution and for evidence of deposit; retain originals and copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — test promptly any preparations IDA sends for authenticity checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Test promptly any preparations the IDA sends for authenticity checking (Guide paragraph 62; Section D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt testing ensures viability confirmation and speedy resolution of discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — converting an existing deposit into a Budapest deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: If converting an existing deposit into a Budapest deposit attend to the specified checklist points (see Guide paragraphs 30–31; 64; Rule 6.4(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion requires following conversion-specific steps including use of BP/4 etc.; consult the Guide for exact points to attend to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — last-minute deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have left making a deposit until the last minute, give priority to sending the microorganism itself to the IDA (Guide paragraphs 29; 61; Rule 6.4(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and paperwork are important but the physical deposit is critical to meet deposit date requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: New deposit — note notification date and calculate deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a new deposit (because original IDA cannot furnish samples), note the date on which you received notification from the IDA of its inability to furnish samples and calculate the latest date by which your new deposit must be made (Guide paragraphs 65–69; 77; Article 4(1)(a),(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely action is required to maintain rights; use the Guide's calculation examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: New deposit — check transfer to substitute IDA / right to make new deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original IDA indicates deposits will be transferred to a substitute IDA under Rule 5.1(a)(i), you may not have the right to make a new deposit (Guide paragraphs 66–69; Article 4(2); Rule 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether a transfer has occurred before preparing a new deposit; if transfer happened you may be precluded from making a new deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: New deposit — documentation to include
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a new deposit include copies of the receipt, the latest viability statement and, where applicable, the latest scientific description/taxonomic designation in respect of the previous deposit; complete and sign the appropriate forms and, unless the forms provide space, append a signed statement giving reason for the new deposit, the date of notification and a declaration that the microorganism is the same as previously deposited (Guide paragraphs 66–82; Rule 6.2(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure enclosures and statements are complete to avoid rejection or delay of the new deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesters — comply with import/quarantine/health/safety before requesting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before requesting a sample, ensure that you have complied with any import, quarantine, health and safety, etc., requirements (Guide paragraph 107).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory and biosafety clearances are the requester's responsibility and must be in place before shipment/receipt of samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting with depositor's authorization (BP/11 route)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you know the identity of the depositor, ask the IDA for WIPO model form BP/11 (if kept), complete parts I, III and IV and send to the depositor to complete part II or write to the depositor asking for a declaration of authorization; then send completed BP/11 or declaration to the IDA with your request and purchase order; pay the fee when requested (Guide paragraphs 90; 93; 94; 101; Rules 11.2(ii) and 11.4(a),(c),(d)(i),(ii); Rule 12.1(a)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is often the simplest route if depositor cooperation is available; ensure depositor signs and authorizes making the material available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting with industrial property office certification (IPO route)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask the IPO or the IDA for the appropriate form, complete the part to be filled in by the requesting party, send it to the IPO for endorsement, then send the endorsed form and any certificate to the IDA together with a purchase order; pay the fee when requested (Guide paragraphs 91; 93; 94; 102; 103; Rules 11.3(a) and 11.4(a),(c),(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This route uses IPO certification to establish entitlement when depositor authorization is not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting an unrestricted deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: To request a sample of a microorganism that is the subject of a granted and published patent, which is available without need for certification, and whose accession number has been communicated to the IDA: write to the IDA with purchase order giving your name and address and quoting the accession number; pay the fee when requested (Guide paragraphs 92–94; 106; Rules 11.3(b) and 11.4(a),(c),(e); Rule 12.1(a)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the straightforward route for post-publication/patent-granted unrestricted deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting a sample for a microorganism subject of a published US patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask the IDA if it is aware the relevant US patent has issued; if yes, proceed as for an unrestricted deposit; if no, include evidence of publication of the US patent with your request, or expect a delay while the IDA verifies publication; pay the fee when requested (Guide paragraphs 92–94; 104–105).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing evidence of US patent publication speeds processing; otherwise IDA verification may delay supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory international forms under the Budapest Treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain international forms are mandatory under the Regulations: receipts for original deposits (BP/4), receipts for new deposits (BP/5), receipts for transfers (BP/6), the viability statement (BP/9) and the form for furnishing samples to parties legally entitled (BP/12) (see Rule references in Appendix 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other BP forms (BP/1,2,3,7,8,10,11,13,14) are model forms and not mandatory; IDAs must use the international forms when mandatory situations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and language of international forms
rubrics_metrics.description: International forms (BP/4,5,6,9) are issued by the competent IDA on the basis of a model established by the WIPO Director General; models are established in English, French, Russian and Spanish, and an IDA may draw up forms in its official language if different (Appendix 3 guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you receive and complete the correct international form in the appropriate language as required by the IDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form BP/12 content and IPO responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Form BP/12 (furnishing of samples to parties legally entitled) is mandatory in content: each IPO may either use Form BP/12 as it appears or draw up its own form with different layout but with contents corresponding to those fixed by the Assembly; the IPO is responsible for the conformity of its form with BP/12; IDAs are not required to verify such conformity (Appendix 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an IPO uses a locally formatted form, ensure its contents match BP/12 requirements to avoid processing issues at the IDA.
